central_question: What will the US 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield (FRED DGS10) be on December 31, 2027, given the current (late October 2026) level near 5.13% and the positively sloped curve, and how do Fed policy/QT, inflation expectations and term premium, Treasury issuance and deficits, foreign official demand, and recession probabilities shape the distribution of outcomes?

situation_brief.current_situation: DGS10 printed 5.13% on 2026-10-21, at the top of its five-year monthly range (1.37% in 2021-09 to 4.989% in 2026-09), with 2s10s at 0.31% and 3M10Y at 0.78% on 2026-10-23. The funds target range stands at 3-3/4 to 4 percent after a 12-0 hike on 2026-09-16. The rise above 5% is driven by real yields and term premium (Kim-Wright term premium 0.96% in 2026-09, top of its five-year range), not by inflation expectations (10-year breakeven 2.351%, 5y5y forward 2.34%).
situation_brief.context: CBO's February 2026 baseline projects a $1.9 trillion FY2026 deficit (5.8% of GDP) averaging $2.4 trillion a year over 2027-2036; Treasury has held nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes unchanged 'for at least the next several quarters' and pushed marginal borrowing into bills. QT ended October 2025 ($2.2 trillion reduction); the Fed has run reserve-management purchases of shorter-term Treasuries since December 2025 with total assets at $6,753,604 millions on 2026-10-21. The September 2026 SEP median funds rate is 4.25% at end-2026 and end-2027, with core PCE medians of 3.4% (2026) and 2.5% (2027).
situation_brief.dynamics: The expected-rate component (roughly 4pp of the ~5% fitted zero-coupon yield) is pinned by a Fed on hold near 4% with market pricing slightly below then above the dots through 2027; the swing factor is the term premium, which has climbed steadily (0.601% Jan 2026 to 0.96% Sep 2026, partial October 1.059%) alongside bill-heavy issuance and large deficits. Recession signals are dormant: the real-time Sahm indicator reads 0.00 percentage points (2026-09) and the Cleveland Fed puts one-year-ahead recession probability at 11.4 percent. Historical base rates from near-5% starts show small moves: 0 of 4 non-overlapping 14-month windows exceeded ±1.0 pp, and the single ±0.5 pp exceedance was downward into the 2007-08 recession.
fault_lines: Term premium at a five-year high (~1%) against deficit/issuance pressure vs Treasury's coupon-size freeze
FOMC reaction function constrained by 3.4% core PCE, not by 4.1% unemployment
Divergent term-premium models: Kim-Wright ~1% vs ACM mirror 0.72-0.73%, implying different expected-rate pricing
Funds futures strip implying a path inconsistent with the 4.25% SEP medians; unresolved wedge
Household inflation expectations (Michigan 1-year at 4.6%) far above near-target market breakevens
Evidence gap: no TIC holdings data for Japan or China and no BoJ policy series in this run

drivers.why_it_matters: Roughly three-fifths of the year's 0.827pp rise in the fitted 10-year yield was compensation, and it sits at its five-year high [S6][S7]

drivers.variable: Federal funds rate path (SEP median vs futures)
drivers.why_it_matters: SEP medians hold the funds rate at 4.25% at end-2026, end-2027 and end-2028 before 3.75% in 2029, anchoring the expected-rate component [S21]

drivers.variable: Federal deficit and Treasury coupon issuance
drivers.why_it_matters: CBO projects deficits averaging $2.4 trillion a year (6.1 percent of GDP) over 2027–2036, pressuring term premium unless absorbed in bills [S11][S27]
Core PCE median of 3.4% for 2026 glides to 2.5% (2027), 2.2% (2028), 2.0% (2029), setting the reaction function [S21][S28]
Runs through the term premium; a persistent marginal-buyer problem produces the steady premium climb observed (0.601% January to 0.96% September 2026) [S6]
A Sahm trigger or rising NY Fed probit would drive rapid cuts and bull flattening of the 0.31% 2s10s [S13][S2][S3]
Anchored near target (2.34% breakeven, 2.2% 5y5y on 2026-10-23), so the swing factor is compensation rather than expected inflation [S4][S5]
QT ended 31 October 2025; reserve-management purchases of shorter-term Treasuries since December 2025 keep the balance sheet flat-to-growing [S29][S17]
